trips.name: Castles to Cathedrals: The Rhine Explorer Ride
trips.summary: Frankfurt to Düsseldorf along the Main and Rhine. Flat, family-friendly, riders aged 10 and up, e-bikes welcome.
trips.details:
## At a glance

Our usual four days: three riding days from Frankfurt to Düsseldorf and one rest day. We fly out on Friday 28 May 2027 after school and work, start riding on Saturday, and are home on Wednesday 2 June. No child misses school, adults take just Tuesday and Wednesday off, and there are four spare days to find the homework.

| | |
|---|---|
| Dates | Arrive Fri 28 May (evening), ride Sat 29 May – Tue 1 June, home Wed 2 June 2027 |
| School days missed | None (Birmingham half term is 31 May – 4 June) |
| Route | Frankfurt – Mainz – Rüdesheim – St Goar – Koblenz – Bonn – Cologne – Düsseldorf, about 275 km along the Main and Rhine |
| Format | Three riding days of 75–100 km, one rest day in Bonn |
| Group | The easy, mixed-ability ride: families welcome, riders aged 10 and up, e-bikes welcome |
| Shorter days | Every day has a train or boat shortcut that cuts it to 45–65 km |
| Terrain | Almost entirely flat, traffic-free riverside path. The biggest climb is the hotel stairs. |
| Travel | You book your own flights: into Frankfurt on Friday evening, home from Düsseldorf on Wednesday |
| Bikes | Your own bike, carried out and back in a lorry the club arranges |

Distances are approximate until the routes are built in RideWithGPS.

## Fitting half term

Birmingham schools are off from Monday 31 May to Friday 4 June 2027 and reopen on Monday 7 June. Monday 31 May is also the spring bank holiday, so adults need only two days of leave, Tuesday and Wednesday. Friday's flight goes after work.

| | Date | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Travel out | Fri 28 May | Evening flight to Frankfurt, after school and work. Aim for flights from about 19:00 |
| Riding | Sat 29 May – Tue 1 June | Two riding days, rest on bank holiday Monday, last riding day Tuesday |
| Travel home | Wed 2 June | Fly home from Düsseldorf |
| Spare days | Thu 3 – Sun 6 June | Room for a delayed flight before school on Monday 7 June |

Academies, free schools and schools outside Birmingham can set their own dates, so please check yours before you register.

## Day by day

The full route is about 275 km, so the riding days are long but flat. Strong riders and teenagers ride every kilometre. Younger children take a train or boat for the dullest flat stretch each day and still ride past all the castles.

| Day | Ride | Full ride | Family option |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fri 28 May | Arrive in Frankfurt | – | Evening flights, bikes already waiting at the hotel. Quick briefing, early night. |
| Sat 29 May | Frankfurt – Mainz – Rüdesheim – St Goar | ~100 km, flat | S-Bahn Frankfurt–Mainz with bikes, then ride ~60 km through the vineyards and into the Rhine Gorge |
| Sun 30 May | St Goar – Loreley – Koblenz – Bonn | ~100 km, flat | KD boat St Goar–Koblenz past the castles, then ride ~65 km to Bonn |
| Mon 31 May | Rest day in Bonn | – | Rhine promenade, Beethoven's birthplace, or a 20-minute train to Cologne cathedral |
| Tue 1 June | Bonn – Cologne – Düsseldorf | ~75 km, flat | Train Bonn–Cologne, then ride ~45 km. Everyone finishes together on Düsseldorf's riverside promenade. |
| Wed 2 June | Home | – | Bikes into the lorry, fly home from Düsseldorf |

The days follow the Rhine cycle route (EuroVelo 15) and the Main path, mostly on traffic-free riverside tracks. Regional trains run alongside the river the whole way, so anyone can stop at any station.

## Riding with children

The youngest riders set the pace for their group, and every day has a way to make it shorter.

- **Ages:** 10 and over. Under-18s ride with a parent or an adult the parents have named in writing, as the Framework requires.
- **Groups:** a dedicated family group or two, each with a leader and a back marker. Adults without children ride in their own groups and wait at the café with the cake.
- **Shortcuts:** the KD Rhine boats between Bingen and Koblenz take bikes when there's room, for about €3.50 per bike per trip. Regional trains run alongside the river all the way to Düsseldorf.
- **Sweep van:** the support van follows the family groups and can carry a tired rider and bike to the next hotel.
- **Kit for children:** a helmet, a bike that has been serviced, a lock, a rain jacket, and the snacks that stop meltdowns.
- **Consent:** every under-18 needs a parental consent and medical form before the trip. We'll send it to you.
- **Rest day in Bonn:** the Rhine promenade, the Haribo shop and a quick train to Cologne cathedral, so nobody needs to sit in a museum.

## Getting there and back

You book your own flights: into Frankfurt on Friday evening 28 May, and home from Düsseldorf on Wednesday 2 June. The club books the hotels. Half-term fares go up quickly, so book early once your place is confirmed.

Your bike travels separately. The bike lorry and its driver leave on Thursday 27 May so the bikes are waiting in Frankfurt, then shadow the route as a second support vehicle and bring them home.

## Where we stay

Five nights in four towns.

| Night | Town |
|---|---|
| Fri 28 May | Frankfurt |
| Sat 29 May | St Goar (or St Goarshausen across the river) |
| Sun 30 and Mon 31 May | Bonn (two nights) |
| Tue 1 June | Düsseldorf |

Rooms are allocated once the hotels confirm. Tell us who you'd like to share with when you register: sharing requests are requests, not promises. A single room costs more than a shared one.

## Before you go

- **Passports:** everyone needs their own, including children. A child travelling with an adult who isn't their parent needs a signed consent letter from the parents.
- **Health cover:** a GHIC or EHIC card plus travel insurance that covers cycling, for adults and children alike.
- **Rhine levels:** spring high water can close sections of the riverside path. We'll check the river forecast the week before and plan diversions.
- **Sunday shopping:** German shops close on Sundays, so stock up on Saturday evening in St Goar. Cafés and bakeries in the wine villages usually open.
- **Path manners:** the Rhine path is busy with families and e-bikes in early June. Use your bell, keep right and ride single file through towns.

## How payment works

Like every W/Rhinos trip, this one runs at cost. You pay a deposit when you register, an interim payment if a hotel needs money before we go, and the final balance after the trip once every cost is known. A flat £50 per rider goes to a charity the riders choose. Details are in the Framework.

trips.name: Capes to Calobra: The Mallorca Explorer Ride
trips.summary: Three riding days from Port de Pollença: Sa Calobra, Lluc, the Orient valley and Cap de Formentor. The "less easy" group, hire bikes on the island, e-bikes welcome.
trips.details:
## At a glance

Four days, one base, no suitcases dragged between hotels. We arrive on Thursday 29 April 2027, ride Friday, Saturday and Monday from Port de Pollença with Sunday off, and everyone is home for Tuesday: one and a half days of annual leave, and a Monday that finally deserves the word "holiday".

| | |
|---|---|
| Dates | Arrive Thu 29 Apr, ride Fri 30 Apr – Mon 3 May 2027 (Mon 3 May is the UK early May bank holiday) |
| Riders | 50–60, the "less easy" group. E-bikes welcome as always |
| Base | Port de Pollença on the north coast: one hotel, four nights (Thu 29 Apr – Mon 3 May) |
| Format | Three riding days and one rest day: two big Tramuntana days, Sunday off, a lighthouse finale before flights |
| Headline rides | Sa Calobra, Lluc, the Orient valley, Cap de Formentor |
| Total riding | Roughly 250 km and 5,000 m of climbing on the long options, with a shorter option every day |
| Bikes | Hire bikes on the island: no bike boxes, no lorry |

Distances and climbing are approximate until the routes are built in RideWithGPS.

## Day by day

The two big days come first while legs are fresh, Sunday is off, and Monday is short and early so nobody misses a flight or a lighthouse.

| Day | Long option | Short option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thu 29 Apr | Arrival | – | Fly in, bike fitting, welcome briefing and dinner |
| Fri 30 Apr | Orient valley: Pollença – Selva – Alaró – Orient – Bunyola – Santa Maria – Inca and home, ~110 km / 1,700 m | Flat north-plain loop via Muro and Santa Margalida, ~65 km / 300 m | A good day to settle into pace groups. Coffee in Orient, lunch in Alaró or Santa Maria |
| Sat 1 May | Sa Calobra: Pollença – Coll de Femenia – Lluc – Coll dels Reis – Sa Calobra and back, ~100 km / 2,400 m | Pollença – Lluc monastery and back, ~50 km / 900 m | Down to Sa Calobra early, before the tour coaches. The 9.5 km climb back out is the day's one real exam |
| Sun 2 May | Rest day | – | Pollença's Sunday market, the Calvari steps for the restless, the beach or a boat to Formentor. Group dinner in the evening |
| Mon 3 May | Formentor: Port de Pollença – Cap de Formentor lighthouse and back, ~40 km / 900 m | Mirador des Colomer and back, ~12 km / 250 m | Wheels rolling 07:30, back by 11:00, bikes handed back by 13:00, afternoon flights |

Anyone who treats the rest day as optional can ride a gentle Cala Sant Vicenç coffee loop (~25 km), but they buy the first round at dinner.

## Riding in groups

Sixty riders in one bunch is a road closure, not a group ride, so we split into five pace groups of 10–12 and stagger the starts.

- **Pace groups:** five groups, each with a ride leader and a back marker. We'll sort the groups before the trip, and you can swap after Friday's ride, no questions asked (and only mild teasing).
- **Starts:** fastest group last, so everyone reaches coffee within about half an hour of each other.
- **Support:** two vans, one mechanic van with the Tramuntana groups and one sweep van for the short options and tired legs.
- **Regroup points:** at the top of every major climb and at key junctions, marked on the RideWithGPS cue sheets.
- **Road rules:** Spain allows riding two abreast and drivers must give 1.5 m. Single file on descents, in villages and whenever a coach appears.
- **Sa Calobra:** it's a dead end, so groups descend in turn and the van waits at the top at Coll dels Reis.
- **Formentor:** nobody races the lighthouse descent. There are goats, and the goats are undefeated.

The W/Rhinos Ride Charter and On the Road one-pager apply, as on every ride.

## Getting there

You book your own flights. There are direct flights from Birmingham, Manchester and East Midlands to Palma. Aim to arrive by Thursday evening and leave from mid-afternoon on Monday. We'll arrange coaches from Palma airport to Port de Pollença (about an hour) for the main arrival and departure times.

## Hire bikes

We hire bikes on the island, delivered to the hotel on Thursday evening and collected on Monday lunchtime.

- **Choose your bike** when you sign up. Expect roughly €100–180 for a carbon road bike for the four days, or about €180–200 for a road e-bike. You pay for the bike you choose.
- **Sizing:** we ask for your height, inside leg, usual frame size and saddle height when you sign up, and send them to the hire shops.
- **Bring your own:** pedals, shoes, helmet, your saddle if you're fussy, bike computer and mount, and bottles.
- **Fitting:** an hour on Thursday evening in the hotel bike room to set saddle heights and fit pedals.
- **Bringing your own bike instead?** You can, but you arrange and pay for flying it yourself.

## Where we stay

One cycle-friendly 4-star hotel in Port de Pollença for everyone, half board, four nights. Rooms are mostly twins with a few singles; tell us who you'd like to share with when you sign up. Sharing requests are requests, not promises, and a single room costs more.

## Early-May watch-outs

- **Formentor traffic:** the car restrictions on the Formentor road only start on 15 May, so on our dates it's open to all traffic. Hence the 07:30 start on Monday: we want to be off the headland by 10:30.
- **Mallorca 312:** the big sportive is the weekend before us (Saturday 24 April 2027). If you want to ride it, you'll need to come out a week earlier.
- **Saturday 1 May is Labour Day in Spain.** Many shops close. Cafés in Lluc and Pollença usually open, and the vans carry food and water just in case.
- **Sa Calobra coaches:** tour coaches use the road from mid-morning. Single file on the hairpins and let them through.
- **Weather:** usually low to mid 20s °C on the coast, cooler and sometimes wet or windy up at Lluc and Coll dels Reis. A gilet and arm warmers go in every back pocket.
- **Insurance:** travel insurance that covers cycling is a must, as on every trip.

## How payment works

Like every W/Rhinos trip, this one runs at cost. You pay a non-refundable deposit once the trip is confirmed, an interim payment if the hotel needs money before we go, and the final balance after the trip once every cost is known. A flat £50 per rider goes to a charity the riders choose.

## Key dates for you

- **By 15 December 2026:** book your flights (arrive Thursday evening, leave Monday from mid-afternoon).
- **By 15 January 2027:** your bike sizes need to be in, so add them on your booking page if you skipped them.
- **By 1 April 2027:** rider brochure, route links and joining pack go out.
